findings.description: §3 says a same-repo issue counts as a spec source as `#N` "or a URL into it", but the CI lock denies `gh issue view*/*`, and every URL contains `/`. A reviewer or validator that runs `gh issue view <URL>` is refused and the read lands in `permission_denials`. §3 should say to pass a same-repo URL on as `#N`. The §7 validator brief has no such hint, unlike review-spec.md L12.

On a local `--fix` run with a spec source (`--spec`, or "fixes #N" in a commit), review-spec reports every unbuilt requirement as `important`. §8 then says to "apply each confirmed finding", which means writing whole features into the working tree. Nothing excludes missing or partial spec findings from auto-fix.

By default, `git status --porcelain` collapses a new untracked directory into a single `?? dir/` line. A local change that adds a new package therefore reaches Shape and the briefs as a directory, with no files and no line counts. `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` lists each file.

`plantCommit`'s doc comment says every case keeps "the head's own message, parents" and that the clean case "looks no different". A spec case now squashes onto `[evalCase.base]` under a bare subject with a `Closes #N.` body, while its clean twin `pr20-clean` keeps the merge parents and the original body. The comment is wrong for spec cases, and no clean case runs the spec reviewer, so its false-positive rate goes unmeasured.

The PR comment's skipped list now excludes spec (`area !== "spec"`), but `reviewersSkipped` in review-metrics.script.ts L186-189 still lists every area absent from the spawn list. So on a PR that closes no issue, the comment omits `spec` while the record's `reviewers_skipped`, which the retro reads, includes it. Deriving "skipped" once would keep the two in step.

Two local-run behaviors unrelated to the spec reviewer ride along: the empty-change stop and the untracked-files inclusion. The untracked-files rule is stated three times (the local change definition, Shape, and the Todo line), so the copies can drift. State it once, in the definition of the change.

The recipe for reading a spec whole (`gh issue view <n> --json title,body,comments`, plus the CI same-repo rule) is written out in review-spec.md L12, SKILL §7's validator brief, SKILL §3 and the workflow lock comment. A change to the command or to the restriction has to edit all of them together. §7 could tell the validator to read the spec the way review-spec does.

The `agents/` row still says 12 agents and "7 `review-*` reviewers + validator". With review-spec there are 13 agents and 8 `review-*` agents (7 reviewers plus the validator), which matches the PR's own update to .claude/README.md. The PR changed "six" to "seven" on L38 of this file but missed this row.

L12 packs the `-R` local-only rule, the CI refusal and the `--comments`-without-body gotcha into one sentence. The colon makes the `--comments` warning read as a consequence of the CI refusal. Split it into two sentences.

The new `Bash(gh issue view*/*)` deny keeps reviewers from reading or quoting another repo's issues, but the existing `Bash(gh pr view*)` and `Bash(gh pr diff*)` allows have no matching deny. So a prompt-injected reviewer can still run `gh pr view -R owner/other-repo N --json body,comments` or `gh pr diff <URL into another repo>`, read another repo's PR with the job token, and quote it into a finding (refuted findings are posted too). Adding `Bash(gh pr view*/*)` and `Bash(gh pr diff*/*)` to deny closes this; no protocol call passes a `/` to either command.

process_issues.description: The correctness instance on the prompt/workflow surfaces ran one read-only `git grep` despite the CI brief allowing only the listed git subcommands. It changed nothing and found no stale wording.
